objective.value: Investigate genome-wide fitness effects of gentamicin on E. coli using a high-resolution CRISPRi screen to understand cellular defense/resistance mechanisms; compare with anaerobic-condition fitness changes; identify regulators (CpxR, ArcA) of respiratory adaptation and membrane depolarization via transcriptomics (iModulon), ChIP-Seq, and membrane potential assays.
objective.notes: Explicit 'In this study, we focused on genome-wide fitness changes induced by gentamicin exposure' plus methods overview.

hypothesis.value: Gentamicin induces fitness changes resembling anaerobic metabolism by disrupting membrane potential (limiting gentamicin uptake); two-component regulators CpxR (and ArcA) mediate respiratory adaptation contributing to gentamicin resistance.

inference.rationale: No single sentence states a formal hypothesis; reconstructed from intro rationale (gentamicin ineffective anaerobically) and abstract/results conclusions.

hypothesis.notes: Intro: understanding anaerobic ineffectiveness 'may shed light on the mechanisms underlying antibiotic resistance'.

value.CRISPRi: sgRNA abundance normalized (Table S2); ER per sgRNA = abundance with dCas9 / initial pool; gene ER = median across targeting sgRNAs; fold-change threshold 1.5; Pearson correlation (r=0.93) and PCA across conditions; COG functional categorization
value.RNA_Seq: CLC Genomics Workbench mapping to NC_000913.3 (length/similarity 0.9); DESeq2 normalization; DEG = >2.0-fold and Padj<0.001; iModulon projection onto P1K structure using pymodulon
value.ChIP_Seq: CLC mapping (0.9/0.9); MACS2 default peak calling; peaks in >=2 replicates = binding events; DOOR2.0 operon assignment
value.growth_assays: Welch's t-test with P<0.1 significance threshold (authors' lenient heuristic, recorded verbatim)
value.membrane_potential: FlowJo v10.2; 100,000 events at 2,000 events/s, FSC threshold 335; red/green fluorescence shift as membrane potential indicator

analysis_methods.notes: P<0.1 Welch's t-test is the authors' stated threshold; recorded verbatim, not reinterpreted.

value.finding: Ribosomal proteins, ribosome-associated proteins and rRNA-modifying enzymes showed increased essentiality (decreased ER) under gentamicin, e.g., rbfA 5.0-fold, yqjD 4.7-fold, rsmD 4.1-fold ER decreases
TA systems affected; antitoxin knockdown more detrimental than toxin knockdown (ghoS 9.8-fold vs ghoT 1.5-fold ER decrease; relB 7.0-fold, yafN 6.7-fold, mazE 3.2-fold, higA 3.0-fold)
OMP (ompA 3.8-fold, bamE 2.6-fold, nlpE 1.8-fold ER decreases) and efflux genes (tolC, acrA, macAB, mdt family) showed reduced ER; bhsA exception with increased ER (3.8-fold under gentamicin)
ER profiles under gentamicin and anaerobic conditions strongly correlate (r=0.93); cofactor biosynthesis genes (rib, ubi, hem pathways, fre, ubiX) showed increased ER under both conditions
Keio deletions of fre, ubiX, ubiC, hemX less gentamicin-sensitive than WT; bhsA deletion conferred complete gentamicin resistance
arcA, arcB, cpxR deletions significantly more sensitive to gentamicin; cpxA deletion had little effect (consistent with CpxR hyperactivation upon cpxA loss, per ref 49)

CpxR bound 933 genomic positions under gentamicin (vs 51 anaerobic, 13 LB), modulating 1,611 genes; binds regulatory regions of nuo, cyo, cyd respiratory operons and arcA; 929/2,348 gentamicin DEGs directly associated with CpxR binding
CpxR represses nuo/cyo/cyd under gentamicin; appCBX (Cyt bd-II) upregulated anaerobically; ArcA activity suppressed under gentamicin (iModulon matches P1K d(arcA))
Membrane potential collapsed under gentamicin in WT but not in the cpxR knockout (DiOC2 flow cytometry; CCCP as uncoupling control)

outcomes.notes: Mechanistic chain (CpxR represses respiration -> membrane depolarization -> reduced gentamicin uptake) is author_interpretation; direct observations are ER values, ChIP binding, expression changes, and flow cytometry.

experiment_instances.purpose: Genome-wide identification of genes affecting fitness under gentamicin and anaerobic conditions
experiment_instances.host: E. coli K-12 MG1655 + pdCas9 + pooled sgRNA library (39,591 spacers)

interventions.detail: High-resolution sgRNA library targeting every 100 bp of CDS; dCas9-mediated repression; pooled competition growth in LB, LB+gentamicin 1 ug/mL, and anaerobic LB

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 yes (active design and construction of a new high-resolution sgRNA library and its deployment); Q2 yes (library designed and constructed in this study per Results and Methods); Q3 yes (the dense 100-bp tiling design choice directly shapes how future fitness screens with this framework are designed).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Construction of an integrated pooled screening platform (library design, cloning, selection, NGS readout) - closest to M11 integrated screening; not a pathway flux intervention.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Most CRISPRi library designs target a single or a few positions per gene, but CRISPRi efficiency varies with genomic structure and dCas9-DNA interactions, making consistent efficiency under all conditions hard to ensure (Results p001).
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Library coverage (39,574/39,591 = 99.96%) and colony counts were directly measured by amplicon sequencing and plating; the design rationale is a procedural observation, not a prediction.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Paper explicitly gives a mechanistic/technical rationale: position- and condition-dependent variation in CRISPRi efficiency motivates dense tiling at 100-bp intervals.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When designing genome-scale CRISPRi fitness screens in E. coli, apply dense sgRNA tiling across every ~100 bp of each CDS with off-target filtering and per-gene median enrichment aggregation, because position- and condition-dependent variation in dCas9 repression efficiency makes single-guide designs unreliable.
alternatives_considered: single- or few-position CRISPRi library designs (rejected: variable efficiency across genomic structures and conditions)

interventions.detail: Gentamicin 1 ug/mL sub-lethal (from dose-response Fig S1) and anaerobic culture as comparison conditions

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 yes (deliberate selection of sub-lethal gentamicin dose and anaerobic condition as experimental interventions); Q2 yes (performed in this study); Q3 yes (dose choice from the dose-response curve determines screening stringency for all downstream ER calls).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Process/condition engineering - selection of cultivation stress conditions rather than a genetic change.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Dose-response curve (Fig S1) identified 1 ug/mL as sub-lethal; literature reports this level induces resistance and stress responses including biofilm formation (ref 17); gentamicin known to be ineffective anaerobically (ref 16).
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Sub-lethal concentration derived from a measured dose-response curve (Fig S1); anaerobic resistance directly observed (Fig S2).
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Paper justifies 1 ug/mL as 'reported to induce resistance and stress responses, including biofilm formation in E. coli (17)' and the anaerobic comparison on prior literature (ref 16); own Fig S1 data support the choice but the stated framing is literature-anchored.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When screening aminoglycoside fitness determinants in E. coli, apply a sub-lethal antibiotic dose chosen from a measured dose-response curve and include an anaerobic condition as a mechanistic comparator, because sub-lethal exposure elicits adaptive stress responses while anaerobiosis phenocopies uptake-blocked resistance.
